This article is complete horseshit and misrepresents the original intentions of the people who made these images. Let me point it out, because this keeps coming up:

These pictures were originally edited and posted in an article by Bulimia.com. Let me say that one more time:

Bulimia.com

For those of you who don't know, bulimia is an eating disorder wherein people abstain from eating for long periods of time because they are obsessed with their body image, and when they do eat, they take drastic countermeasures afterwards (such as inducing vomiting). People with bulimia are extremely overweight and have a distorted view of what "normal" body weight is.

The reason a website revolving around bulimia would make an article showing fatter versions of female video game characters should be abundantly clear. It has nothing to do with feminism, as much as other news sources that have given the article attention would like to have you believe.

To spell it out for you, it's an attempt to normalize higher body weight to sufferers of bulimia, in order to help them overcome their obsession with having as little body weight as possible.

I personally think the original article was still kind of fucky, but it's nowhere near as bad as everybody is making it out to be. It's got nothing to do with obese feminists trying to make fat the new "normal", and has everything to do with a support website for bulemics trying to prevent dangerously underweight people with an eating disorder from killing themselves slowly with malnutrition.
